findings.source_quote: ἡμεῖς τὸ βοηθούμενον, „σὺ ὁ βοηθός“, „ὁ ἰατρός“, „ὁ σωτήρ“, „τὸ τεῖχος“, ἡ ζωή, „ἡ ἐλπίς“, „ἡ καταφυγή“, ἡ χαρά, ἡ προσδοκία.
findings.english_quote: We are those who receive help; you are the helper, the physician, the Savior, the wall, the life, the hope, the refuge, the joy, the expectation, and the rest.
findings.issue: The words survive, but the selected edition’s six separately marked quotations have been absorbed into an unmarked enumeration. The outer quotation marks around the entire prayer do not preserve the distinction between these quoted expressions and the intervening unquoted attributes.
findings.suggested_revision: Restore inner quotation boundaries around “you are the helper,” “the physician,” “the Savior,” “the wall,” “the hope,” and “the refuge,” using single quotation marks inside the quoted prayer. Keep the other attributes outside those inner quotations. This is preservation of the supplied editorial presentation, not a textual correction.

findings.issue: In an enumeration, “and the rest” ordinarily means the unspecified remainder of the list. Here ἀνάπαυσις names rest or repose as another divine attribute; it is not a catch-all expression. The English introduces an avoidable ambiguity absent from this Greek noun.
findings.suggested_revision: Replace “and the rest” with “and rest” or “and repose,” making this a distinct predicate rather than an unspecified remainder. The revised wording requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: Μέλλων ἐπὶ τὴν Τύρον ὁρμᾶν μεθ’ ἡμέρας ἑπτὰ βούλομαι ἐξ αὐτῆς ὑμᾶς ἀπελθόντας
findings.english_quote: The feminine pronoun occurs twice without an explicit feminine antecedent in this excerpt.
findings.issue: The disclosure is overbroad: Tyre is an explicit feminine antecedent candidate immediately before the first ἐξ αὐτῆς. What is absent is an explicit antecedent naming the current city required by the chosen spatial interpretation. The lexical note also calls Tyre “subsequently named,” although it has already been named here. Furthermore, the ensuing journey to Tyre is compatible with both the contextual spatial reading and the idiomatic temporal reading “at once”; it does not by itself establish their relative likelihood. The spatial main rendering remains a defensible contextual choice, but its supporting disclosure needs correction.
findings.suggested_revision: Revise both notes to explain that Tyre precedes the first occurrence, while the main translation instead supplies an implicit reference to the current city. Explicitly retain the idiomatic alternative “at once” for both occurrences and explain that the ensuing journey is compatible with either interpretation. Remove the inaccurate word-order statement and qualify the comparative-likelihood claim. No source correction or print verification is required; the revised disclosure must undergo fresh review.
